cards.front: New hypertension after 20 weeks' gestation with proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction is [___].
cards.context: Define it by timing + multisystem involvement: new hypertension after 20 weeks PLUS proteinuria or any other end-organ dysfunction (renal, hepatic, neurological, haematological, or fetal). Delivery is the only cure.

cards.front: APGAR components (each 0-2, total 0-10): [___] (colour), Pulse, Grimace (reflex), Activity (tone), Respiration. Assessed at 1 minutes after birth and again at 5 minutes.
cards.context:
APGAR is a 5-component bedside assessment at 1 and 5 min (and q5min if low).

It documents the infant's condition and response to resuscitation — it does NOT trigger resuscitation, which is guided by breathing, heart rate and tone assessed within seconds of birth (AAP/ACOG).

The ranges (7-10 vigorous, 4-6 moderately depressed, 0-3 severely depressed) describe status, not a resuscitation recipe.

cards.front: Australian stillbirth rate is approximately [___] per 1000 births; about 20-30% are considered potentially preventable.
cards.context:
Australia's stillbirth rate (~7 per 1000) has barely moved in two decades despite gains elsewhere in maternal-fetal medicine.

The 20-week / 400g threshold (Australian/AIHW definition; WHO uses ≥28 weeks / ≥1000g for international comparison) separates stillbirth from late miscarriage.

That a fifth to a third are potentially preventable is the rationale behind the Safer Baby Bundle — the flat rate reflects missed modifiable risks (FGR, smoking, supine sleep), not an unavoidable floor.

cards.front: Universal (rather than ethnicity-based) core reproductive carrier screening covers cystic fibrosis, [___], and fragile X.
cards.context:
Most affected children are born to couples without a family history, and self-reported ethnicity poorly predicts carrier status. RANZCOG therefore recommends offering screening regardless of background.

The core panel covers three conditions; expanded screens cover many more. If both partners are carriers, options can include PGT-M with IVF, donor gametes or prenatal diagnosis.

cards.front: Given to a woman in threatened preterm labour to mature the fetal lungs, antenatal [___] reduce respiratory distress.
cards.context: The single most effective intervention in threatened preterm birth: a maternal steroid course matures fetal lungs (surfactant), cutting respiratory distress, intraventricular haemorrhage, and death. Effect peaks ~48h.

cards.front: Endometriosis work-up uses pelvic [___] or MRI; consider laparoscopy when imaging is negative and empirical treatment is unsuccessful or inappropriate.
cards.context:
Use pelvic ultrasound or MRI in the diagnostic work-up for endometriosis, while recognising that negative imaging does not exclude superficial peritoneal disease.

Consider laparoscopy when imaging is negative and empirical treatment is unsuccessful or inappropriate; when lesions are sampled at laparoscopy, histology helps confirm the diagnosis. CA-125 is non-specific.

Modern practice: empirical medical therapy first (NSAIDs + continuous COC/progestin → dienogest → GnRH agonists with add-back HRT); laparoscopy for diagnostic uncertainty, treatment failure, or fertility concerns.

cards.front: In hyperemesis gravidarum, give IV thiamine before any [___] to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy (triad: confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia).
cards.context:
Wernicke encephalopathy from acute thiamine deficiency strikes thiamine-dependent metabolic steps in the brainstem + cerebellum.

Catastrophic interaction: glucose pushes pyruvate down a thiamine-requiring step that's already starved → accelerates the lesion, risks permanent Korsakoff amnesia.

Cost trivial; harm of skipping is irreversible memory loss — same rule in alcoholic patients.

cards.front: Neonatal seizures present subtly (lip-smacking, eye deviation, cycling limb movements, apnoea) rather than as classic tonic-clonic activity. The most common cause is [___] (~60%), treated with therapeutic hypothermia within 6 h.
cards.context:
Neonatal seizures present differently from older children's because the immature brain has limited capacity for generalised tonic-clonic activity.

HIE accounts for ~60% and is treatable with therapeutic hypothermia within 6 h — every minute matters.

Workup: BGL (hypoglycaemia → 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg) and electrolytes (Ca, Mg, Na) — all reversible causes. First-line phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg IV loading; pyridoxine trial for refractory.

cards.front: In neonatal resuscitation, the priority for a non-breathing baby is lung [___] (positive-pressure breaths), before compressions.
cards.context:
Two newborn-specific principles: a baby who isn't breathing needs effective lung inflation (positive-pressure breaths) FIRST — not chest compressions.

Term resuscitation starts in air (21%), not 100% oxygen, to avoid oxidative injury.

cards.front: APH is bleeding from the genital tract from 20+0 weeks until birth; affects 3-5% of pregnancies; never perform [___] VE until praevia excluded.
cards.context:
The 20-week threshold separates APH from threatened miscarriage; bleeding once labour has started is relabelled intrapartum haemorrhage.

Two safety rules drive the workup. First, stabilise the mother before chasing the cause: large-bore access, FBC + coag + group-and-hold, fetal assessment, and anti-D if Rh-negative.

Second, no digital vaginal exam until ultrasound has excluded placenta praevia — probing a low-lying placenta can provoke catastrophic haemorrhage.

cards.front: Signs of neonatal respiratory distress: tachypnoea >[___]/min, grunting, nasal flaring, recession, cyanosis. Any neonate with these signs needs urgent assessment.
cards.context:
Five classic signs of neonatal respiratory distress: tachypnoea (>60/min), grunting (partial glottis closure for auto-PEEP), nasal flaring, intercostal/subcostal recession, cyanosis.

Combinations escalate urgency (Silverman-Andersen score quantifies).

Differential by gestation + context: TTN (term/near-term post-CS, self-limiting), RDS (preterm, ground-glass CXR), pneumothorax (often after MAS/PPV), MAS (post-term, meconium-stained liquor, patchy infiltrates).

cards.front: The classic triad of ruptured ectopic pregnancy is amenorrhoea, vaginal bleeding, and unilateral [___].
cards.context:
The classic triad occurs in only about half of ectopic pregnancies; presentations may include GI symptoms, shoulder-tip pain or syncope.

Risk rises after previous ectopic, tubal damage or surgery, IVF, or pregnancy with an IUD in situ. Assess with TVUS and serial βhCG; an empty uterus above the local threshold is concerning but not diagnostic.

Rupture with instability needs urgent surgery. Stable, eligible patients with low βhCG and no fetal cardiac activity may be considered for methotrexate.

cards.front: Active neonatal resuscitation: not routinely recommended <24 weeks; offered at family discretion in the borderline window; recommended ≥[___] weeks.
cards.context:
Thresholds for active resuscitation reflect survival + disability outcomes at each gestation. Below 23 weeks: virtually no survivors with intact neurology (palliative comfort care).

At 23 weeks: very low survival (~30-40% at best, many with moderate-severe disability) — individualised decision; at 24 weeks: ~50-70% survival.

cards.front: Cord prolapse: position the patient in Trendelenburg or knee-chest and elevate the presenting part; if vaginal birth is not imminent, expedite [___] birth.
cards.context:
Cord prolapse can rapidly compromise fetal oxygenation. Immediately use steep Trendelenburg or knee-chest and manually elevate the presenting part.

If vaginal birth is not imminent, expedite caesarean birth: category 1 for a suspicious or pathological fetal heart rate; category 2 may be considered with a normal trace.

For prolonged transfer, bladder filling with 500-750 mL saline can maintain elevation. Minimise cord handling to avoid vasospasm.

cards.front: Small for gestational age (SGA) = estimated fetal weight (EFW) <10th centile; fetal growth restriction (FGR) is pathological, usually <[___]rd centile or abnormal Dopplers.
cards.context:
The trap: SGA is a size label, FGR is a diagnosis of failed growth potential.

SGA just means EFW <10th centile. Many are constitutionally small but healthy (small parents, female fetus), needing only surveillance to confirm normal velocity with normal Dopplers.

FGR is the pathological subset, flagged by centile <3rd OR abnormal umbilical artery Dopplers signalling placental insufficiency. Doppler separates the at-risk fetus from the merely small one and drives delivery.

cards.front: Earliest sign of magnesium toxicity is loss of [___] reflexes (~5 mmol/L); antidote is IV calcium gluconate.
cards.context:
Magnesium toxicity follows a dose-response cascade you can monitor at the bedside without lab access. Therapeutic level is 2-4 mmol/L (anticonvulsant action).

Loss of patellar reflexes appears at ~5 mmol/L — the earliest reliable warning. Respiratory depression follows at ~6-7 mmol/L.

Cardiac conduction abnormalities and arrest at ~12 mmol/L.

cards.front: In antepartum haemorrhage, NEVER perform digital vaginal exam until placenta praevia is excluded by [___]; speculum is safe but VE risks catastrophic bleeding.
cards.context:
A finger through the cervical os of a placenta praevia can shear the placental edge directly → catastrophic haemorrhage within seconds.

Workup: maternal history + vitals → speculum to visualise cervix + bleeding source (safe — doesn't enter os) → transabdominal USS to localise placenta.

cards.front: Brief intubation to give surfactant then immediate extubation to CPAP is called [___].
cards.context: INSURE (INtubate, SURfactant, Extubate to CPAP) minimises ventilation time. The infant is intubated only briefly to deliver the surfactant dose, then extubated back to nasal CPAP.

cards.front: Male factor contributes to about 50% of infertile couples; diagnosis requires [___] abnormal semen analyses.
cards.context:
Male factor is the sole or contributing cause in roughly 50% of infertility cases. Testing the woman first and the man only if 'nothing comes up' misses half the diagnoses and delays treatment.

Standard practice is parallel workup: female cycle history + day 2-5 hormones + ovulation confirmation + tubal patency, alongside male history + semen analysis from the start.

Two semen samples are required before diagnosing male factor because count, motility, and morphology fluctuate substantially day-to-day from illness, fever, abstinence period, and stress.

cards.front: In vasa praevia, fetal mortality exceeds 50% if undiagnosed, but falls below [___]% with elective caesarean at 35-36 weeks.
cards.context:
Vasa praevia: unprotected fetal vessels run across the cervical os — through membranes (Type 1, velamentous cord) or between placental lobes (Type 2, succenturiate/bilobed).

Undiagnosed mortality >50%; diagnosed + planned delivery (elective CS at 35-36 weeks before ROM) reduces to <5%.

Classical undiagnosed: painless bleeding at ROM + sinusoidal FHR → emergency CS.
